title: No verifier membership without a valid split
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $C,c$ be natural numbers, and let $y$ be a binary string. If the bounded search for an integer $n$ with $n+C\cdot 2^{(n+1)^c}=|y|$ returns no value, then $y$ does not belong to the choice-word verifier language for $N,C,c$.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet
the split search at $|y|$ returns no value
replaced: Let $N$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine and $C, c$ natural numbers. If the exponential split search fails at the length of a string $y$, then $y$ is not in the exponential choice-word verifier language of $N$ with parameters $C, c$.
